title: simon-notes-p8 card N3 still listed sewage sludge on the 1996 Protocol's Annex 1 permitted list after Resolution LP.6(17) removed it
authority: PRIMARY, reused from CORR-LP617-SEWAGE-SLUDGE-20261028 (no new source research for this proposition). (1) Resolution LP.6(17), adopted 7 October 2022 by the Seventeenth Meeting of Contracting Parties to the 1996 Protocol, Annex: Annex 1 paragraph 1 'Delete sub-paragraph 1.2 ... .2 sewage sludge; Renumber the subsequent sub-paragraphs'; operative: no new permits for dumping sewage sludge after entry into force; active permits may be maintained until the expiry date, but not later than 31 May 2027. Registered as SRC-IMO-LP6-17. (2) Status of IMO Treaties Vol. II, 30 September 2026: the 2022 amendments entered into force on 15 January 2023 under Article 22.4. Registered as SRC-IMO-STATUS-TREATIES-VOL2-2026-09-30.
rationale: Follow-up B of known_traps entry 141, opened by CORR-LP617-SEWAGE-SLUDGE-20261028 and scheduled by the Founder on 30 Oct 2026 as a separately governed correction. Card N3 ('1996 Protocol - Permitted Reverse List (Annex 1)') listed sewage sludge first among the permitted materials, contradicting the corrected QB1_A Q13. Sewage sludge is removed from the list; a new line states its deletion by LP.6(17), adopted 7 October 2022 and in force 15 January 2023, and the permit rule (no new permits; existing permits not beyond 31 May 2027); the reg-box gains the LP.6(17) row used on QB1_A Q13; the N3 stamp moves v1.0 -> v1.1 (the simon-notes-p5 N8 precedent of 5 Aug 2026).

It remains a recorded, uncorrected derived surface pending a separately governed refresh. (b) Six statements on N3 (entry 141's verification items B1 and B2 plus four further items) verified at primary source on 30 Oct 2026 - 'mining waste' and the incomplete Annex 1 list, Annex 4 / LP.4(8) presented as if in force, the 2019 attribution of CO2 export, the 2006 amendment labelled LP.4(8), the Protocol 'replacing' the Convention, and the Protocol's Annex 3 given as evaluation criteria - are first-instance propositions with no parent record, so they cannot be carried by this propagation entry; they are a separately proposed correction.
